newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares inch higher at end, Astra soars.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares inch higher at end, Astra soars.

text.p: Swedish share prices advanced on Tuesday after drug company Astra soared in late trade following an announcement about the patents for its blockbusting anti-ulcer drug, Losec.
The stock exchange's general index rose 0.19 percent to 2,801.91 in turnover totalling 3.9 billion crowns.

Astra leapt 16.5 crowns to 336.5 after the company announced the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) updated its approved drugs list with another three patents for Losec, a move seen as strengthening Losec's patents.
But some players downplayed the significance of the change.

"We really don't see any reason to trade the share up like this but it seems like many traders had been short in the share ahead of the Fed's meeting this evening. That is probably the explanation behind the rally," one broker said.
Trade was otherwise sidelined ahead of the outcome of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting.
Nordbanken jumped nine crowns to 249. The banking sector has lagged behind the broad market lately, brokers said. Swedbank fell 3.5 crowns to 149 and Handelsbanken rose 2.5 crowns to 222.
Kinnevik rose one crown to 210.5 after the media and investment company said that its profit after financial items fell to 159 million crowns, down from 423 million in the same 1996 period.
